questions.text: अम्लीय माध्यम में MnO4⁻ के साथ SO3²⁻ के ऑक्सीकरण का उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: The product of oxidation of SO3²⁻ with MnO4⁻ in acidic medium is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) SO4²⁻. In acidic medium, MnO4⁻ is a strong oxidising agent. When SO3²⁻ (sulphite ion, where sulphur is in +4 oxidation state) is oxidised by MnO4⁻ in acidic medium, sulphur is oxidised from +4 to +6 oxidation state, giving SO4²⁻ (sulphate ion). Options (A) SO2 represents reduction, (C) S²⁻ is a reduced form of sulphur, and (D) S2O3²⁻ is thiosulphate which is not the product of this oxidation.
questions.topic: Oxidation reactions of sulphur compounds

questions.text: [Co(en)3]³⁺ में Co की उपसहसंयोजन संख्या है :
questions.text_english: The coordination number of Co in [Co(en)3]³⁺ is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 6. In [Co(en)3]³⁺, 'en' stands for ethylenediamine (H2N–CH2–CH2–NH2), which is a bidentate ligand — it donates two lone pairs to the central metal ion. There are three 'en' ligands, each providing 2 donor atoms. Therefore, the total number of coordinate bonds = 3 × 2 = 6. Thus, the coordination number of Co is 6. Options (A), (B), and (C) are incorrect because they do not account for the bidentate nature of 'en'.
questions.topic: Coordination number of complexes with bidentate ligands

questions.text: निम्नलिखित संकुलों में से कौन-सा अनायनीकृत है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following complexes is non-ionisable ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) [Co(NH3)3Cl3]. A complex is non-ionisable when all the ligands (including the halide ions) are present inside the coordination sphere (within the square brackets) and there are no ions outside it. In [Co(NH3)3Cl3], the coordination number of Co is 6 (3 NH3 + 3 Cl), all within the coordination sphere, and there are no counter ions outside it. Hence it is a non-electrolyte and does not ionise in solution. Options (B), (C), and (D) all have Cl⁻ ions outside the coordination sphere and thus produce ions in solution.
questions.topic: Ionisation in coordination complexes

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा बेन्ज़िलिक हैलाइड है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is a benzylic halide ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). A benzylic halide is one in which the halogen atom is attached to the carbon that is directly bonded to the aromatic ring (the benzylic carbon). In option (B), the halogen X is on the carbon directly attached to the benzene ring, making it a benzylic halide. Option (A) has the halogen on a carbon that is two carbons away from the ring (homobenzylic), option (C) also qualifies as benzylic but option (B) is the classic primary benzylic structure shown, and option (D) has halogen on the secondary carbon one position away from the ring.
questions.topic: Types of alkyl halides — benzylic halides

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसकी तुलना में फ़ीनॉल कम अम्लीय है ?
questions.text_english: Phenol is less acidic than :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) o-nitrophenol. Phenol is more acidic than ethanol, o-methoxyphenol, and o-methylphenol because the electron-withdrawing resonance effect of the benzene ring stabilises the phenoxide ion. However, o-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol because the nitro group (–NO2) is a strong electron-withdrawing group that further stabilises the phenoxide ion through inductive and resonance effects, making phenol less acidic in comparison. Ethanol is less acidic than phenol, and o-methoxyphenol and o-methylphenol with electron-donating groups are also less acidic than phenol.
questions.topic: Acidity of phenols — effect of substituents

questions.text: HI के साथ अभिक्रिया करके (CH3)3C–O–CH3 देता है :
questions.text_english: (CH3)3C–O–CH3 reacts with HI to give :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (CH3)3C–I + CH3OH. When an unsymmetrical ether reacts with HI, the cleavage occurs such that I⁻ attacks the more substituted (tertiary) carbon via an SN1 mechanism, while the less substituted side leaves as an alcohol. In (CH3)3C–O–CH3, the tertiary carbon of the t-butyl group forms a stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by I⁻ to give (CH3)3C–I, and the methoxy group leaves as CH3OH. Option (B) would require both groups to be converted to iodides, which occurs only with excess HI and on further heating; option (C) and (D) show incorrect attack at the less substituted carbon.
questions.topic: Cleavage of ethers with HI

questions.text: ऐस्पिरिन निम्न में से किसके ऐसीटिलन से निर्मित होती है ?
questions.text_english: Aspirin is formed by the acetylation of :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Salicylic acid. Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is prepared by the acetylation of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) with acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst. The –OH group of salicylic acid reacts with the acetic anhydride to form the acetyl ester, yielding aspirin. Benzoic acid has no –OH group to acetylate; phenol gives phenyl acetate, not aspirin; and phthalic acid is not involved in the synthesis of aspirin.
questions.topic: Drugs — analgesics, aspirin synthesis

questions.text: दो द्रवों के स्थिरक्वाथी विलयन का क्वथनांक उन दोनों द्रवों के क्वथनांक से उच्चतर होता है जब यह :
questions.text_english: An azeotropic solution of two liquids has boiling point higher than either of them when it :

options.B: shows positive deviation from Raoult's law
options.C: shows negative deviation from Raoult's law
options.D: shows no deviation from Raoult's law

options_english.B: shows positive deviation from Raoult's law
options_english.C: shows negative deviation from Raoult's law
options_english.D: shows no deviation from Raoult's law

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. When a solution shows negative deviation from Raoult's law, the intermolecular attractive forces between the components are stronger than in the pure liquids, resulting in a lower vapour pressure than expected. This lower vapour pressure means a higher boiling point. Such azeotropes have a maximum boiling point (e.g., HNO3–water mixture). Positive deviation leads to a minimum boiling point azeotrope; saturated solutions and ideal solutions (no deviation) do not form azeotropes with elevated boiling points by this mechanism.
questions.topic: Azeotropes — positive and negative deviation from Raoult's law

questions.text: जलीय CuCl2 के विद्युत-अपघटन के दौरान :
questions.text_english: During electrolysis of aqueous CuCl2 :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Cu is formed at cathode. During electrolysis of aqueous CuCl2, Cu²⁺ ions migrate to the cathode where they are reduced (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu), forming solid copper metal. At the anode, Cl⁻ ions are oxidised in preference to water (due to overvoltage effects and concentration), liberating Cl2 gas. Therefore, H2 is not liberated at the cathode (option A is wrong), O2 is not liberated at the anode (option C is wrong), and Cl2 is liberated at the anode, not cathode (option D is wrong).
questions.topic: Electrolysis — products at electrodes

questions.text: किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया की अर्ध-आयु 1386 सेकण्ड है । अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक (k) है :
questions.text_english: Half-life period of a first order reaction is 1386 seconds. The rate constant (k) of the reaction is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 0.5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. For a first order reaction, t₁/₂ = 0.693/k. Therefore k = 0.693/t₁/₂ = 0.693/1386 = 0.0005 s⁻¹ = 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ = 0.5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Options (B), (C), and (D) give incorrect values that do not satisfy the relation k = 0.693/1386.
questions.topic: First order reaction — half-life and rate constant

questions.text: किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के जलीय विलयन के वाष्प दाब का आपेक्षिक अवनमन 0.0225 है । अवाष्पशील विलेय का मोल-अंश है :
questions.text_english: The relative lowering of vapour pressure of an aqueous solution containing non-volatile solute is 0.0225. The mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 0.0225. According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure equals the mole fraction of the solute: (P° – P)/P° = x_solute. Since the relative lowering of vapour pressure is given as 0.0225, the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is directly 0.0225. This is a direct application of Raoult's law for non-volatile solutes, and no further calculation is required. Options (A), (B), and (C) are incorrect.
questions.topic: Relative lowering of vapour pressure — Raoult's law

questions.text: अभिक्रिया 2A + B2 → 2AB के लिए अभिक्रिया वेग दिया गया है वेग = k[A]²[B2]. वेग स्थिरांक (k) का मान बढ़ाया जा सकता है :
questions.text_english: The rate of the reaction 2A + B2 → 2AB is given by Rate = k[A]²[B2]. The value of rate constant (k) can be increased by :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) increasing the temperature. The rate constant (k) is a characteristic of a reaction that depends only on temperature, as described by the Arrhenius equation: k = Ae^(–Ea/RT). Increasing temperature increases k exponentially. Changing the concentrations of A or B affects the rate of reaction but does NOT change the rate constant k. Therefore options (A), (B), and (D) are incorrect.
questions.topic: Rate constant — dependence on temperature (Arrhenius equation)

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों का विरचन गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण द्वारा किया जा सकता है ।

Assertion (A) : Aromatic primary amines can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R) : Alkyl halide undergoes nucleophilic substitution with anion formed by phthalimide.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 के लिए, दो कथन दिए गए हैं — जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

Assertion (A) is FALSE: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis cannot be used to prepare aromatic primary amines because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reactions under normal conditions (they are less reactive in SN reactions). The synthesis is used only for aliphatic primary amines. Reason (R) is TRUE: alkyl halides do undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion (formed by treatment with KOH). Since the assertion is false but the reason is true, option (D) is correct.

कारण (R) : RNA स्वप्रतिकरण करता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Uracil base is present in RNA.
Reason (R) : RNA undergoes self-replication.

options.A: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, R is false
options.D: A is false, R is true

options_english.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, R is false

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Assertion (A) is TRUE: Uracil is indeed one of the four nitrogenous bases found in RNA (instead of thymine which is found in DNA). Reason (R) is FALSE: It is DNA, not RNA, that undergoes self-replication (semi-conservative replication). RNA does not self-replicate under normal biological conditions. Since the assertion is true but the reason is false, option (C) is correct.

कारण (R) : ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीनों के डाइऐज़ोनियम लवण अनुनाद दर्शाते हैं ।

Assertion (A) : Diazonium salts of aliphatic amines are more stable than those of aromatic amines.
Reason (R) : Diazonium salts of aromatic amines show resonance.

options.A: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, R is false
options.D: A is false, R is true

options_english.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, R is false
options_english.D: A is false, R is true

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Assertion (A) is FALSE: Diazonium salts of aliphatic amines are highly unstable and decompose rapidly even at low temperatures, while diazonium salts of aromatic amines are comparatively more stable due to resonance stabilisation with the benzene ring. Reason (R) is TRUE: Aromatic diazonium salts are stabilised by resonance as the positive charge is delocalised over the benzene ring, making them more stable. Since assertion is false but reason is true, option (D) is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐनिलीन की अपेक्षा ऐसेटेनिलाइड (C6H5–NHCOCH3) कम क्षारकीय होता है ।
कारण (R) : ऐनिलीन के ऐसीटिलन के कारण ऐसेटेनिलाइड में नाइट्रोजन पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व घट जाता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Acetanilide (C6H5–NHCOCH3) is less basic than aniline.
Reason (R) : Acetylation of aniline results in decrease of electron density on nitrogen in acetanilide.

options.A: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, R is false
options.D: A is false, R is true

options_english.A: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation of A
options_english.B: Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, R is false
options_english.D: A is false, R is true

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Acetanilide is less basic than aniline because in acetanilide, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen is delocalised into the carbonyl group of the acetyl moiety (–COCH3) through resonance, reducing the electron density on nitrogen. This makes the lone pair less available for donation to a proton (H⁺), thereby decreasing its basicity. The acetylation (introduction of the –COCH3 group) is precisely the reason for this electron density decrease, so Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.topic: Basicity of amines — effect of acetylation

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised in the human body in adequate amounts and must therefore be supplied through the diet. Examples include valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, and threonine.

It consists of three components joined together: a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine), a pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), and one or more phosphate groups. sub_questions.text: यौगिकों के निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन-सा यौगिक अधिक तीव्रता से SN1 अभिक्रिया करता है और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which compound undergoes SN1 reaction faster and why ? C6H5–CH2Cl OR cyclohexyl–CH2Cl

key_points: C6H5–CH2Cl (benzyl chloride) reacts faster via SN1
The benzyl carbocation formed is stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring

sub_questions.solution: C6H5–CH2Cl (benzyl chloride) undergoes SN1 reaction faster. In the SN1 mechanism, the rate-determining step is the formation of a carbocation intermediate. When C6H5–CH2Cl ionises, it forms the benzyl carbocation (C6H5–CH2⁺), which is highly stabilised by resonance with the adjacent phenyl ring. The positive charge is delocalised over the ring. Cyclohexylmethyl chloride forms a primary carbocation with no such resonance stabilisation. Therefore, benzyl chloride reacts much faster by SN1.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में मुख्य उत्पाद लिखिए : cyclohexane + Br2, UV प्रकाश →
sub_questions.text_english: Write the major product in the following : cyclohexane + Br2, UV light →

key_points: Bromocyclohexane (cyclohexyl bromide)
Free radical halogenation replaces one H with Br

sub_questions.solution: The major product is bromocyclohexane (C6H11Br). In the presence of UV light, Br2 undergoes homolytic cleavage to generate bromine free radicals, which then abstract a hydrogen atom from cyclohexane to form a cyclohexyl radical. This radical reacts with another Br2 molecule to give bromocyclohexane and a new Br radical, propagating the chain. Since all the hydrogen atoms in cyclohexane are equivalent, only one monosubstitution product is formed.

questions.text:
किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक 1.25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ है । इस अभिकर्मक के 5 g को 2.5 g में घटने में कितना समय लगेगा ?
[ log 2 = 0.301, log 3 = 0.4771, log 4 = 0.6021 ]
questions.text_english:
A first order reaction has a rate constant 1.25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. How long will 5 g of this reactant take to reduce to 2.5 g ?
[ log 2 = 0.301, log 3 = 0.4771, log 4 = 0.6021 ]
questions.solution: For a first order reaction: t = (2.303/k) × log([A]0/[A]t). Here, [A]0 = 5 g, [A]t = 2.5 g, k = 1.25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Therefore, t = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10⁻³) × log(5/2.5) = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10⁻³) × log 2 = 1842.4 × 0.301 = 554.5 seconds. Thus the reactant takes approximately 554.5 seconds (≈ 554 s) to reduce from 5 g to 2.5 g.
questions.topic: First order reaction — time calculation

sub_questions.text: लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is lanthanoid contraction ?

key_points: Steady decrease in atomic/ionic radii of lanthanoids from La to Lu
Caused by poor shielding of 4f electrons

sub_questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction is the steady and regular decrease in atomic and ionic radii observed across the lanthanoid series from lanthanum (La) to lutetium (Lu). This occurs because, as the atomic number increases, electrons are added to the inner 4f subshell. The 4f electrons provide poor shielding of the nuclear charge, so the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outermost electrons increases, causing the electron cloud to contract.

sub_questions.text: ऐक्टिनॉयड आकुंचन लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन से अधिक क्यों होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction. Why ?

key_points: 5f electrons of actinoids have even poorer shielding than 4f electrons of lanthanoids
Greater effective nuclear charge increase per element in actinoids

sub_questions.solution: Actinoid contraction is greater than lanthanoid contraction because the 5f electrons in actinoids have even poorer shielding effect than the 4f electrons in lanthanoids. The 5f orbitals are more diffuse and have a greater radial extent, but their shielding of one another is less effective. Therefore, across the actinoid series, the increase in effective nuclear charge per added electron is larger, leading to a greater contraction in size from element to element compared to the lanthanoids.

questions.text: यूरिया (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 60 g mol⁻¹) का 4% विलयन किसी अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ के 5.2% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है । अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ का अणु भार परिकलित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A 4% solution of urea (molar mass = 60 g mol⁻¹) is isotonic with 5.2% solution of an unknown organic substance. Calculate the molecular weight of the unknown organic substance.

key_points: Isotonic solutions have equal osmotic pressure, hence equal molar concentrations
w1/M1 = w2/M2 (for same volume of solution)

questions.solution: Two solutions are isotonic when they have the same osmotic pressure, which means they have the same molar concentration (molarity). For the same volume of solution (100 g of solution approximated to 100 mL), the number of moles per unit volume must be equal. Therefore: (w1/M1) = (w2/M2), which gives 4/60 = 5.2/M2. Solving: M2 = (5.2 × 60)/4 = 312/4 = 78 g mol⁻¹. The molecular weight of the unknown organic substance is 78 g mol⁻¹.
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure — isotonic solutions

questions.text:
ताप में 17°C से 27°C तक वृद्धि करने पर किसी गैसीय अभिक्रिया का वेग तीन गुना हो जाता है । इस अभिक्रिया के लिए सक्रियण ऊर्जा का परिकलन कीजिए ।
[ दिया गया है : 2.303 R = 19.15 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 3 = 0.48 ]
questions.text_english:
The rate of a gaseous reaction triples when temperature is increased from 17°C to 27°C. Calculate the energy of activation for this reaction.
[Given : 2.303 R = 19.15 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 3 = 0.48]

key_points: Use Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = Ea/2.303R × (T2–T1)/(T1×T2)

questions.solution: Using the Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = Ea/(2.303R) × (T2 – T1)/(T1 × T2). Here T1 = 17 + 273 = 290 K, T2 = 27 + 273 = 300 K, k2/k1 = 3 (rate triples), and 2.303R = 19.15 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Substituting: log 3 = Ea/19.15 × (300 – 290)/(290 × 300). Therefore 0.48 = Ea/19.15 × 10/87000. Solving: Ea = 0.48 × 19.15 × 87000/10 = 0.48 × 19.15 × 8700 = 79,916.4 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 79.9 kJ mol⁻¹. The activation energy for the reaction is approximately 79.9 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.topic: Arrhenius equation — activation energy calculation

questions.text:

Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.1 M) || Sn²⁺(0.001 M) | Sn(s)
दिया गया है : E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V, E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0.14 V
[ log 10 = 1 ]
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell :
Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.1 M) || Sn²⁺(0.001 M) | Sn(s)
Given : E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0.76 V, E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0.14 V
[ log 10 = 1 ]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.14 – (–0.76) = +0.62 V
Nernst equation: E = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q

questions.solution: Step 1 — Standard EMF: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = E°(Sn²⁺/Sn) – E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = (–0.14) – (–0.76) = +0.62 V. Step 2 — Reaction quotient Q: The cell reaction is Zn + Sn²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Sn. Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Sn²⁺] = 0.1/0.001 = 100. Step 3 — Nernst equation (n = 2): E = E° – (0.0591/2) × log Q = 0.62 – (0.02955) × log 100 = 0.62 – (0.02955 × 2) = 0.62 – 0.0591 = 0.5609 V ≈ 0.56 V. The EMF of the cell is approximately 0.56 V.

questions.text: 283 K पर किसी विलायक का वाष्प दाब 100 mm Hg है । उस तनु विलयन का वाष्प दाब परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें 283 K पर किसी प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य AB का 1 मोल विलायक के 50 मोल में घुला है (यह मान लीजिए कि विलेय AB पूर्णतः वियोजित हो जाता है) ।
questions.text_english: The vapour pressure of a solvent at 283 K is 100 mm Hg. Calculate the vapour pressure of a dilute solution containing 1 mole of a strong electrolyte AB in 50 moles of the solvent at 283 K (assuming complete dissociation of solute AB).

key_points: AB dissociates completely into A⁺ and B⁻, giving 2 moles of ions per mole
Total moles of solute particles = 2
Total moles = 2 + 50 = 52
Mole fraction of solvent = 50/52

questions.solution: Since AB is a strong electrolyte and completely dissociates: AB → A⁺ + B⁻, 1 mole of AB gives 2 moles of ions. Total moles of solute particles = 2. Moles of solvent = 50. Total moles in solution = 50 + 2 = 52. Mole fraction of solvent = 50/52. By Raoult's law: P = x_solvent × P° = (50/52) × 100 = 5000/52 = 96.15 mm Hg. Therefore the vapour pressure of the solution is approximately 96.15 mm Hg.

Write the reaction involved in the following :

sub_questions.text: वोल्फ-किश्नर अपचयन
sub_questions.text_english: Wolff-Kishner reduction

key_points: Carbonyl compound reacts with hydrazine to form hydrazone
Hydrazone treated with KOH/ethylene glycol at high temperature gives alkane

sub_questions.solution: In the Wolff-Kishner reduction, the carbonyl group (C=O) of an aldehyde or ketone is reduced to a methylene group (–CH2–). The carbonyl compound first reacts with hydrazine (H2N–NH2) to form a hydrazone (C=N–NH2). The hydrazone is then heated with a strong base (KOH) in ethylene glycol at high temperature (200°C), leading to the replacement of the C=O by –CH2–. Example: RCHO + H2N–NH2 → RCH=N–NH2 → (KOH, heat) → RCH3.

sub_questions.text: विकार्बोक्सिलन अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Decarboxylation reaction

key_points: Carboxylic acid salt (sodium salt) heated with soda lime gives alkane with loss of CO2

sub_questions.solution: Decarboxylation is the reaction in which a carboxylic acid loses a carbon dioxide molecule (CO2) to give an alkane. When the sodium or calcium salt of a carboxylic acid is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO), decarboxylation occurs. Example: CH3COONa + NaOH → (CaO, heat) → CH4 + Na2CO3. Here, sodium acetate loses CO2 and is converted to methane.

sub_questions.text: कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
sub_questions.text_english: Cannizzaro reaction

key_points: Aldehydes without alpha hydrogen undergo disproportionation with conc. NaOH
One molecule is oxidised to carboxylate salt, another is reduced to alcohol

sub_questions.solution: The Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction exhibited by aldehydes that have no alpha (α) hydrogen atoms. When treated with concentrated NaOH, one molecule of the aldehyde is oxidised to the carboxylic acid (as its sodium salt), while another molecule is simultaneously reduced to the corresponding alcohol. Example: 2HCHO + NaOH → HCOONa + CH3OH (formaldehyde gives sodium formate and methanol). Similarly, 2C6H5CHO + NaOH(conc.) → C6H5COONa + C6H5CH2OH.

sub_questions.solution: Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is prepared from phenol by the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl3) and aqueous NaOH; electrophilic substitution by the dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) intermediate occurs predominantly at the ortho position, and subsequent hydrolysis gives the aldehyde group: C6H5OH + CHCl3 + NaOH → 2-HO-C6H4-CHO (salicylaldehyde) + 3NaCl + H2O.

sub_questions.solution: 2-Methoxyacetophenone is prepared by Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole. Anisole is treated with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 (Lewis acid catalyst). The methoxy group (–OCH3) is an activating ortho/para director. The major product formed is 2-methoxyacetophenone (ortho isomer) along with some para isomer: C6H5OCH3 + CH3COCl → (AlCl3) → 2-CH3CO-C6H4-OCH3 + HCl.

H2SO4) → C6H2(NO2)3OH + 3H2O.

questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Chlorine is ortho/para directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, though chlorine is an electron withdrawing group.
(b) Racemic mixture is optically inactive.
(c) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride.

sub_questions.text: क्लोरीन यद्यपि इलेक्ट्रॉन अपनयक समूह है फिर भी ऑर्थो/पैरा निर्देशक है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Chlorine is ortho/para directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, though chlorine is an electron withdrawing group.

key_points: Cl withdraws electrons inductively (–I effect) but donates via resonance (+M effect)
Lone pairs on Cl are donated to the ring by resonance, activating ortho and para positions
Net effect: ring is deactivated overall but o/p positions are preferentially activated by resonance

sub_questions.solution: Chlorine has two opposing electronic effects on the benzene ring. By the inductive effect (–I effect), Cl withdraws electrons from the ring, making it less reactive overall. However, chlorine also donates one of its lone pairs of electrons to the ring by the resonance (+M or mesomeric) effect. This resonance donation specifically increases the electron density at the ortho and para positions relative to the meta position. Although the ring is overall deactivated, the ortho and para positions are relatively more electron-rich than the meta positions. Hence, electrophilic attack preferentially occurs at ortho and para positions, making Cl an ortho/para director despite being electron withdrawing.

sub_questions.text: रेसिमिक मिश्रण ध्रुवण अघूर्णक होता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Racemic mixture is optically inactive.

key_points: Racemic mixture is an equimolar mixture of d and l enantiomers
The equal and opposite optical rotations cancel each other out (external compensation)

sub_questions.solution: A racemic mixture (racemate) consists of equal molar proportions of the two enantiomers (d-form and l-form) of an optically active compound. Each enantiomer rotates the plane of plane-polarised light by an equal amount but in opposite directions — the d-form rotates it clockwise and the l-form rotates it anticlockwise. Since the magnitudes of rotation are equal and opposite, they exactly cancel each other out (external compensation). As a result, the net rotation of the racemic mixture is zero and it is optically inactive.

sub_questions.text: n-प्रोपिल क्लोराइड की अपेक्षा ऐलिल क्लोराइड अधिक शीघ्रता से जल-अपघटित हो जाता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride.

key_points: Allyl chloride forms a resonance-stabilised allylic carbocation on ionisation
The allylic carbocation is highly stable, facilitating SN1 hydrolysis
n-propyl chloride gives an unstabilised primary carbocation

sub_questions.solution: Allyl chloride (CH2=CH–CH2Cl) is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride (CH3CH2CH2Cl) because of the greater stability of the carbocation intermediate formed. When allyl chloride ionises, it gives an allylic carbocation (CH2=CH–CH2⁺ ↔ ⁺CH2–CH=CH2) that is stabilised by resonance — the positive charge is delocalised over two carbon atoms via the adjacent double bond. n-propyl chloride, on the other hand, gives an ordinary primary carbocation with no such resonance stabilisation. The greater stability of the allylic carbocation lowers the activation energy for the ionisation step, making allyl chloride undergo SN1 hydrolysis much faster.

questions.text_english: Transition metals have incomplete d-subshell either in neutral atom or in their ions. The presence of partly filled d-orbitals in their atoms makes transition elements different from that of the non-transition elements. With partly filled d-orbitals, these elements exhibit certain characteristic properties such as display of a variety of oxidation states, formation of coloured ions and entering into complex formation with a variety of ligands. The transition metals and their compounds also exhibit catalytic properties and paramagnetic behaviour. The transition metals are very hard and have low volatility. An examination of the E°(M²⁺/M) values shows the varying trends : [Table: V = –1.18, Cr = –0.91, Mn = –1.18, Fe = –0.44, Co = –0.28, Ni = –0.25, Cu = +0.34, Zn = –0.76]

sub_questions.text: किस आधार पर हम कह सकते हैं कि Cu एक संक्रमण तत्व है लेकिन Zn नहीं ? (परमाणु क्रमांक : Cu = 29, Zn = 30)
sub_questions.text_english: On what basis can we say that Cu is a transition element but Zn is not ? (Atomic number : Cu = 29, Zn = 30)

key_points: Cu (Z=29): [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹; Cu²⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d⁹ — incomplete d-subshell in ion
Zn (Z=30): [Ar]3d¹⁰4s²; Zn²⁺ has configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰ — completely filled d-subshell in all states

sub_questions.solution: A transition element is defined as one that has an incomplete d-subshell in its ground state or in any of its commonly occurring oxidation states. Cu (Z=29) has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹. In its most common ionic state Cu²⁺, its configuration is [Ar]3d⁹ — an incomplete d-subshell. Therefore Cu qualifies as a transition element. Zn (Z=30) has configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s². In its ionic state Zn²⁺, configuration is [Ar]3d¹⁰ — a completely filled d-subshell. Since Zn never has an incomplete d-subshell in any state, it is not a transition element.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण तत्व ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं में विविधता क्यों दर्शाते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why do transition elements show variety of oxidation states ?

key_points: (n–1)d and ns orbitals are very close in energy
Electrons from both d and s orbitals can participate in bonding
Different numbers of electrons can be involved, giving different oxidation states

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements show a variety of oxidation states because in these elements, the (n–1)d and ns orbitals are very close in energy. Electrons from both the outermost s orbital and the penultimate d orbitals can be used for bonding. As the energy difference between these orbitals is small, different numbers of d electrons can be involved in bond formation, resulting in multiple and variable oxidation states. For example, manganese shows oxidation states ranging from +2 to +7.

sub_questions.text:
(i) वैनेडियम से ज़िंक तक E°(M²⁺/M) के मान अनियमित प्रवृत्ति क्यों दर्शाते हैं ?
(ii) संक्रमण धातुओं में ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं की परिवर्तनीयता असंक्रमण तत्वों की परिवर्तनीयता से किस प्रकार भिन्न होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Why do E°(M²⁺/M) values show irregular trend from Vanadium to Zinc ?
(ii) How is the variability in oxidation states of transition metals different from that of the non-transition elements ?

key_points: (i) Irregular E° values due to irregular variations in ionisation enthalpies, sublimation enthalpies, and hydration enthalpies across the series
(ii) Transition metals show consecutive oxidation states differing by 1 (e.g., Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺) using d electrons; non-transition metals change by 2 (s electrons) and their states are non-consecutive

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The E°(M²⁺/M) values show irregular trend from V to Zn because these values depend on three energy contributions: ionisation enthalpy (energy to remove electrons), sublimation enthalpy (energy to convert solid metal to gaseous atoms), and hydration enthalpy (energy released when ions are hydrated). All three quantities vary irregularly across the transition series due to the irregular filling of 3d orbitals, resulting in an irregular trend in E° values.

(ii) In transition metals, variability in oxidation states arises from the involvement of both ns and (n–1)d electrons in bonding. The oxidation states change by one unit at a time (e.g., +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7 for Mn), and consecutive states are common. In non-transition elements (s-block), only ns electrons are used for bonding, so the oxidation state usually changes in steps of 2 (e.g., Sn²⁺/Sn⁴⁺), and intermediate states are generally not stable.

questions.text: कार्बोहाइड्रेट पौधों और प्राणियों दोनों में जीवन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं । पौधों में स्टार्च की तरह और प्राणियों में ग्लाइकोजन के रूप में कार्बोहाइड्रेट संग्रहण अणुओं की भाँति प्रयुक्त होते हैं । रासायनिक रूप से ये पॉलिहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड अथवा कीटोन होते हैं । कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को जल-अपघटन में उनके व्यवहार के आधार पर मोनोसैकैराइड, ओलिगोसैकैराइड और पॉलिसैकैराइड में वर्गीकृत किया गया है । सभी मोनोसैकैराइड अपचायी शर्करा होती हैं, अर्थात् ये टॉलेन अभिकर्मक तथा फेलिंग विलयन से ऑक्सीकृत हो जाती हैं । ग्लूकोस जैसा मोनोसैकैराइड ऐल्डोहैक्सोज होता है और इसका आण्विक सूत्र C6H12O6 पाया गया । विभिन्न अभिकर्मकों जैसे HI, H2N–OH, ब्रोमीन जल, (CH3CO)2O इत्यादि के साथ अभिक्रिया करके इसकी संरचना में एक ऐल्डिहाइड समूह, एक प्राथमिक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (–CH2OH) और चार द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (>CHOH) पाए गए । ऐल्डिहाइड समूह उपस्थित होते हुए भी ग्लूकोस ऐल्डिहाइड समूह की कुछ अभिक्रियाएँ जैसे शिफ परीक्षण, NaHSO3 योगज नहीं देता है । यह ग्लूकोस के दो चक्रीय हैमीऐसीटैल रूपों के अस्तित्व को समझाता है जिनमें भिन्नता केवल C–1 पर उपस्थित हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह के विन्यास में होती है ।
questions.text_english: Carbohydrates are essential for life in both plants and animals. Carbohydrates are used as storage molecules as starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Chemically they are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. On the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, i.e., they are oxidized by Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. A monosaccharide like glucose is aldohexose and its molecular formula was found to be C6H12O6. After reacting with different reagents like HI, H2N–OH, Bromine water, (CH3CO)2O, etc. its structure was found to contain one aldehyde group, one primary alcoholic group (–CH2OH) and four secondary alcoholic groups (>CHOH). Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give some of the reactions of aldehyde group like Schiff's test, NaHSO3 addition. This explains the existence of glucose in two cyclic hemiacetal forms which differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C–1.

sub_questions.text: अपचायी शर्करा क्या होती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: What are reducing sugars ?

key_points: Sugars that reduce Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution
They have a free aldehyde or ketone group (or potential to form one)

sub_questions.solution: Reducing sugars are carbohydrates that can reduce mild oxidising agents such as Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) and Fehling's solution (alkaline CuSO4). They possess a free aldehyde group (–CHO) or a free ketone group (or a hemiacetal group that can open to give an aldehyde). All monosaccharides are reducing sugars. Among disaccharides, maltose and lactose are reducing sugars, but sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

sub_questions.text_english: Classify the following into monosaccharide and disaccharide : Fructose, Sucrose, Lactose, Galactose

key_points: Monosaccharides: Fructose, Galactose
Disaccharides: Sucrose, Lactose

sub_questions.solution: Monosaccharides (cannot be hydrolysed further): Fructose and Galactose. Both are simple sugars with molecular formula C6H12O6. Disaccharides (yield two monosaccharide units on hydrolysis): Sucrose and Lactose. Sucrose on hydrolysis gives glucose + fructose; Lactose on hydrolysis gives glucose + galactose.

sub_questions.text_english: Name the polysaccharide which is known as 'animal starch'. Why is it called 'animal starch' ?

key_points: Glycogen is called animal starch
It is stored in animal tissues (liver and muscles) just as starch is stored in plants

sub_questions.solution: Glycogen is the polysaccharide known as 'animal starch'. It is called animal starch because it serves as the energy storage polysaccharide in animals, performing the same function as starch does in plants. Glycogen is stored in the liver and muscle tissues of animals and is mobilised when the body requires energy. Like starch, glycogen is a polymer of glucose units, but it is more highly branched. Just as plants store glucose in the form of starch, animals store glucose in the form of glycogen — hence the name 'animal starch'.

sub_questions.text_english: The resistance of 0.05 M CH3COOH solution is found to be 100 ohm. If the cell constant is 0.0354 cm⁻¹, calculate the molar conductivity of the acetic acid solution.

key_points: κ = cell constant / R = 0.0354/100 = 3.54 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹

sub_questions.solution: Step 1 — Calculate conductivity (κ): κ = cell constant / resistance = 0.0354 cm⁻¹ / 100 Ω = 3.54 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹. Step 2 — Calculate molar conductivity (Λm): Λm = (κ × 1000) / M = (3.54 × 10⁻⁴ × 1000) / 0.05 = 0.354 / 0.05 = 7.08 S cm² mol⁻¹. Therefore the molar conductivity of the 0.05 M acetic acid solution is 7.08 S cm² mol⁻¹.

key_points: Faraday's first law: mass of substance deposited is proportional to quantity of electricity passed
MnO4⁻ → Mn²⁺: Mn changes from +7 to +2, a change of 5 electrons per Mn
1 mole of MnO4⁻ requires 5 Faradays of charge

sub_questions.solution:
Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis: The mass of a substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (charge) passed through the electrolyte.

For the reduction of MnO4⁻ to Mn²⁺: MnO4⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H2O. In this half-reaction, the oxidation state of Mn changes from +7 (in MnO4⁻) to +2 (in Mn²⁺), a change of 5. Therefore, 5 electrons are required per MnO4⁻ ion, meaning 1 mole of MnO4⁻ requires 5 Faradays (5 × 96500 C) of charge.

sub_questions.text: अष्टफलकीय संकुल की Δo और चतुष्फलकीय संकुल की Δt में संबंध
sub_questions.text_english: How is Δo related to Δt ?

key_points: Δt = (4/9)Δo

sub_questions.solution: The crystal field splitting energy for a tetrahedral complex (Δt) is related to that of an octahedral complex (Δo) by the expression: Δt = (4/9)Δo. This means the splitting in a tetrahedral field is approximately 4/9 (or about 44%) of that in an octahedral field for the same metal and same ligands. This smaller splitting in tetrahedral complexes occurs because there are only 4 ligands (instead of 6) and they do not point directly at any d orbital.

sub_questions.text: [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2 का IUPAC नाम
sub_questions.text_english: Write the IUPAC name of [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2

key_points: Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate

sub_questions.solution: The IUPAC name of [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2 is Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate. In the complex ion [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺, Pt has an oxidation state of +4 (since 2Cl each –1 and two neutral en ligands give +4 for Pt to balance the 2+ charge). The ligands are named alphabetically: chlorido (Cl⁻) and ethane-1,2-diamine (en). NO3⁻ is the counter anion, named nitrate.

sub_questions.text: VBT के आधार पर [Ni(CO)4] की ज्यामिति और चुंबकीय व्यवहार
sub_questions.text_english: Write the geometry and magnetic behaviour of [Ni(CO)4] on the basis of VBT.

key_points: Ni in [Ni(CO)4] is in 0 oxidation state; configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s⁰ after pairing
sp³ hybridisation — tetrahedral geometry
Diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons)

sub_questions.solution: In [Ni(CO)4], nickel is in the zero oxidation state with configuration [Ar]3d⁸4s². Since CO is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of the two 4s electrons into 3d orbitals, giving Ni the configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰. The empty 4s and three 4p orbitals undergo sp³ hybridisation to accommodate the four CO ligands. The geometry is tetrahedral. Since all 3d electrons are paired (d¹⁰), the complex is diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons, zero magnetic moment).

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] द्वारा किस प्रकार की समावयवता
sub_questions.text_english: What type of isomerism is shown by [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] ?

key_points: Coordination isomerism — the ligands exchanged between cationic and anionic complexes

sub_questions.solution: The complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows coordination isomerism. In this type of isomerism, the ligands of the cationic and anionic coordination entities interchange between them. The coordination isomer would be [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], where the NH3 and CN⁻ ligands have swapped between the two metal centres. This is possible because both Co and Cr can form stable coordination complexes with both NH3 and CN⁻ ligands.

sub_questions.text: d⁴ आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास यदि Δo < P
sub_questions.text_english: Electronic configuration for d⁴ ion if Δo < P. High spin or low spin ?

key_points: When Δo < P, electrons prefer to occupy higher energy eg orbitals rather than pair in t2g
Electronic configuration: t2g³ eg¹ (one electron in each of the four d orbitals)
High spin complex with 4 unpaired electrons

sub_questions.solution: When Δo < P (pairing energy), the energy required to pair electrons is greater than the crystal field splitting energy. Therefore, electrons avoid pairing and occupy the higher eg orbitals singly before pairing in t2g. For a d⁴ ion with Δo < P, the electronic configuration is t2g³ eg¹, with 4 unpaired electrons (one in each d orbital). This is a high spin complex. High spin complexes result from weak field ligands where the crystal field splitting is insufficient to force electron pairing.

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ और [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ में से कौन हेट्रोलेप्टिक संकुल है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ and [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺, which complex is heteroleptic and why ?

key_points: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ is heteroleptic
It has two different types of ligands: NH3 and Cl⁻

sub_questions.solution: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ is the heteroleptic complex. A heteroleptic complex is one in which the central metal ion is bonded to two or more different types of ligands. In [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺, Co is coordinated to both NH3 (neutral ligand) and Cl⁻ (anionic ligand) — two different kinds. In contrast, [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ is a homoleptic complex because Co is surrounded by only one type of ligand (NH3) throughout its coordination sphere.

sub_questions.text: [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ के प्रकाशिक समावयवों की संरचनाएँ
sub_questions.text_english: Draw the structures of optical isomers of [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺

key_points: [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ is an octahedral complex (Pt is +4, with 2 Cl⁻ and 2 bidentate en)
The trans isomer (trans-[PtCl2(en)2]²⁺) has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive
The cis isomer (cis-[PtCl2(en)2]²⁺) has no plane of symmetry and exists as d and l optical isomers

sub_questions.solution: In [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ (octahedral, Pt⁴⁺), the cis isomer (where the two Cl⁻ are on the same side) lacks a plane of symmetry and is chiral, giving rise to two non-superimposable mirror image structures — the d (dextrorotatory) and l (laevorotatory) optical isomers. The trans isomer (where the two Cl⁻ are on opposite sides) possesses a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive (achiral). So [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ shows optical isomerism only for the cis configuration. The structures are two mirror-image forms of the cis complex where the arrangement of the en ligand and Cl groups around the Pt centre are non-superimposable.

sub_questions.solution: Oxidation of aldehydes is easier than that of ketones because aldehydes possess a hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl carbon (the –CHO group). This hydrogen is relatively easy to remove by an oxidising agent, allowing aldehydes to be oxidised to carboxylic acids even with mild oxidising agents like Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. Ketones have no such hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon (the C=O is flanked by two carbon groups), so oxidation would require breaking a carbon–carbon bond, which needs much stronger conditions. Hence ketones are resistant to mild oxidation.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों के ऐल्फा (α) हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय होती है ।
sub_questions.text_english: The alpha (α) hydrogen atoms of aldehydes are acidic in nature.

key_points: Carbonyl group (C=O) withdraws electron density by inductive and resonance effects
The α–C–H bond is weakened, making the α hydrogen removable as H⁺
Resulting carbanion (enolate) is resonance-stabilised

sub_questions.solution: The alpha (α) hydrogen atoms of aldehydes are acidic in nature because the carbonyl group (C=O) adjacent to the α-carbon has a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect and resonance effect. These effects reduce the electron density on the α-carbon, weakening the α–C–H bond. As a result, the α-hydrogen can be removed as a proton (H⁺) by a base relatively easily. The carbanion (enolate ion) formed after the removal of α-hydrogen is stabilised by resonance between the α-carbon and the carbonyl oxygen. This resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base makes the α-hydrogen measurably acidic.

sub_questions.text: (1) Acetophenone + NaOH/I2 → ? (2) Benzoyl chloride + (CH3)2Cd → ?
sub_questions.text_english: Write the products in the following reactions : (1) Acetophenone + NaOH/I2 (2) Benzoyl chloride + (CH3)2Cd

key_points: (1) Iodoform reaction: C6H5COCH3 + NaOH/I2 → CHI3 (iodoform) + C6H5COONa
(2) Corey-House: C6H5COCl + (CH3)2Cd → C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone) + CdCl2

sub_questions.solution:
(1) Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) reacts with NaOH/I2 via the iodoform reaction. The methyl ketone undergoes triiodomethylation of the –CH3 group, followed by cleavage to give iodoform (CHI3, yellow precipitate) and sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa). C6H5COCH3 + 3I2 + 3NaOH → C6H5COONa + CHI3 + 3NaI + 2H2O.

(2) Benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) reacts with dimethylcadmium [(CH3)2Cd] in a Corey-House type reaction. Organocadmium reagents react with acid chlorides to give ketones. The product is acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) and cadmium chloride (CdCl2). C6H5COCl + (CH3)2Cd → C6H5COCH3 + CdCl2.

sub_questions.text: एथेनॉइक अम्ल और ऐथेनैल में विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण
sub_questions.text_english: Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between ethanoic acid and ethanal.

key_points: Tollens' test: Ethanal gives silver mirror with Tollens' reagent; ethanoic acid does not
Or: NaHCO3 test: ethanoic acid gives brisk effervescence (CO2); ethanal does not

sub_questions.solution: A simple test to distinguish ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) from ethanal (CH3CHO) is the Tollens' test (silver mirror test). When treated with Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate solution), ethanal reduces the silver ions to metallic silver, producing a shiny silver mirror on the inside of the test tube. Ethanoic acid, being a carboxylic acid and not an aldehyde, does not reduce Tollens' reagent and gives no silver mirror. Alternatively, ethanoic acid gives brisk effervescence with NaHCO3 solution (releasing CO2), while ethanal gives no such reaction.
